scenes.text: It's July 1324, and you're riding into Cairo with more gold than anyone has seen.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: busy street in medieval Cairo, 1324: sandstone houses with carved wooden balconies, minarets, market awnings, palm trees, bright sun

scenes.text: Behind you walk thousands of people, many of them carrying gold.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: busy street in medieval Cairo, 1324: sandstone houses with carved wooden balconies, minarets, market awnings, palm trees, bright sun

scenes.text: You hand it out to officials, to beggars, to anyone who asks.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: busy street in medieval Cairo, 1324: sandstone houses with carved wooden balconies, minarets, market awnings, palm trees, bright sun

scenes.text: A few months later, you'll be borrowing money in this same city, at high interest.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: busy street in medieval Cairo, 1324: sandstone houses with carved wooden balconies, minarets, market awnings, palm trees, bright sun

scenes.text: And seven hundred years later, the internet will call you the richest person who ever lived.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: busy street in medieval Cairo, 1324: sandstone houses with carved wooden balconies, minarets, market awnings, palm trees, bright sun

scenes.text: Your gold even changes what gold is worth in Egypt.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: busy street in medieval Cairo, 1324: sandstone houses with carved wooden balconies, minarets, market awnings, palm trees, bright sun

scenes.text: By the end, you'll know the one money rule that got you here, and whether it still works today.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: busy street in medieval Cairo, 1324: sandstone houses with carved wooden balconies, minarets, market awnings, palm trees, bright sun

scenes.text: But to get here, we have to go back. It's about 1280, and you're born in Mali.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African family compound, about 1280: round mud-brick houses, thatched roofs, a courtyard with a mortar and pestle

scenes.text: Your name is Musa. Keep count of two things: the gold, and the debts.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Mali is a young empire in West Africa, founded by your great-uncle's family.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Its first great ruler was Sunjata. You're from his family, but not first in line.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your family name says you're royal. It doesn't say you'll ever rule.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Kings in Mali are called mansa: the word just means ruler.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The empire is huge: it stretches from the Atlantic coast deep into the Sahara.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It controls the trade routes where salt from the north meets gold from the south.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You grow up a Muslim, like most of the royal court.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You learn Arabic, the language of trade and religion across the desert.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Arabic will matter later. It lets you talk directly to Cairo.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Now, the gold. Mali sits near some of the biggest gold fields of the medieval world.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African gold field near a river, about 1300: shallow pits in red earth, wooden bowls for washing gravel, river bank, baobab trees, morning light

scenes.text: Miners dig shallow pits in the red earth and wash the gravel in wooden bowls.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African gold field near a river, about 1300: shallow pits in red earth, wooden bowls for washing gravel, river bank, baobab trees, morning light

scenes.text: Gold dust from these fields travels north, on camels, to North Africa and Europe.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African gold field near a river, about 1300: shallow pits in red earth, wooden bowls for washing gravel, river bank, baobab trees, morning light

scenes.text: Here's the surprising part: the king doesn't actually own the mines.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African gold field near a river, about 1300: shallow pits in red earth, wooden bowls for washing gravel, river bank, baobab trees, morning light

scenes.text: The miners keep digging, and pay the king a share, as long as he leaves them alone.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African gold field near a river, about 1300: shallow pits in red earth, wooden bowls for washing gravel, river bank, baobab trees, morning light

scenes.text: Later writers say kings who tried to take over the mines saw the gold dry up.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African gold field near a river, about 1300: shallow pits in red earth, wooden bowls for washing gravel, river bank, baobab trees, morning light

scenes.text: So the gold comes from fields you don't control. Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African gold field near a river, about 1300: shallow pits in red earth, wooden bowls for washing gravel, river bank, baobab trees, morning light

scenes.text: The king does keep every gold nugget. Merchants may only trade the dust.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African gold field near a river, about 1300: shallow pits in red earth, wooden bowls for washing gravel, river bank, baobab trees, morning light

scenes.text: Which is a nice rule to have when you're the king.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African gold field near a river, about 1300: shallow pits in red earth, wooden bowls for washing gravel, river bank, baobab trees, morning light

scenes.text: Salt from the desert is so scarce here that it trades almost weight for weight with gold, some writers claim.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African gold field near a river, about 1300: shallow pits in red earth, wooden bowls for washing gravel, river bank, baobab trees, morning light

scenes.text: That last one is probably exaggerated, but salt really is precious in the south.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African gold field near a river, about 1300: shallow pits in red earth, wooden bowls for washing gravel, river bank, baobab trees, morning light

scenes.text: By about 1310, you're a trusted man at the royal court.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: royal court of the Mali Empire, about 1300: large round mud-brick audience hall with a thatched roof, carved wooden stools, drums, silk canopy, courtyard

scenes.text: The mansa on the throne has one obsession: the ocean.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: royal court of the Mali Empire, about 1300: large round mud-brick audience hall with a thatched roof, carved wooden stools, drums, silk canopy, courtyard

scenes.text: He wants to know what's on the other side of the Atlantic.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: royal court of the Mali Empire, about 1300: large round mud-brick audience hall with a thatched roof, carved wooden stools, drums, silk canopy, courtyard

scenes.text: So he sends two hundred ships west. Only one comes back.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African Atlantic coast, about 1311: wide beach with hundreds of long wooden canoes pulled up on the sand, palm trees, open grey ocean

scenes.text: Its captain says the others sailed into a strong current and vanished.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African Atlantic coast, about 1311: wide beach with hundreds of long wooden canoes pulled up on the sand, palm trees, open grey ocean

scenes.text: Most kings would take that as a no. This one builds a bigger fleet.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African Atlantic coast, about 1311: wide beach with hundreds of long wooden canoes pulled up on the sand, palm trees, open grey ocean

scenes.text: Two thousand ships, some for men, some for food and water.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African Atlantic coast, about 1311: wide beach with hundreds of long wooden canoes pulled up on the sand, palm trees, open grey ocean

scenes.text: And this time, he goes himself. He leaves you in charge until he returns.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African Atlantic coast, about 1311: wide beach with hundreds of long wooden canoes pulled up on the sand, palm trees, open grey ocean

scenes.text: He never returns.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African Atlantic coast, about 1311: wide beach with hundreds of long wooden canoes pulled up on the sand, palm trees, open grey ocean

scenes.text: So you become mansa of Mali. Remember how you got the job.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African Atlantic coast, about 1311: wide beach with hundreds of long wooden canoes pulled up on the sand, palm trees, open grey ocean

scenes.text: The internet calls that sailor king Abubakari the Second, and says he reached America.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African Atlantic coast, about 1311: wide beach with hundreds of long wooden canoes pulled up on the sand, palm trees, open grey ocean

scenes.text: The only source is your own story, told later in Cairo. It doesn't even name him.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African Atlantic coast, about 1311: wide beach with hundreds of long wooden canoes pulled up on the sand, palm trees, open grey ocean

scenes.text: Some historians think the voyage was real. Others think you simply took the throne.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African Atlantic coast, about 1311: wide beach with hundreds of long wooden canoes pulled up on the sand, palm trees, open grey ocean

scenes.text: Either way, you're king now, and he isn't.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: West African Atlantic coast, about 1311: wide beach with hundreds of long wooden canoes pulled up on the sand, palm trees, open grey ocean

scenes.text: As mansa, you sit under a silk canopy, and nobody speaks to you directly.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: royal court of the Mali Empire, about 1300: large round mud-brick audience hall with a thatched roof, carved wooden stools, drums, silk canopy, courtyard

scenes.text: People throw dust on their heads before they talk to you: a sign of respect.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: royal court of the Mali Empire, about 1300: large round mud-brick audience hall with a thatched roof, carved wooden stools, drums, silk canopy, courtyard

scenes.text: Your generals push the empire east, to the trading city of Gao on the Niger River.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: mud-brick trading town on the Niger River, 1320: flat roofs, market stalls, river boats

scenes.text: In Cairo, you'll later claim to have conquered twenty-four cities.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Gold tax, salt tax, copper trade: money pours into your treasury.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You picture all of it piled in one place.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But in your faith, a king with this much has a duty: the pilgrimage to Mecca.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It's called the hajj, and every Muslim who can afford it should go once.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You can afford it. Very, very much.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The day you run out of money in Cairo is about twelve years away.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Before you pack, let's talk about what gold is actually worth.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: village market fair with food stalls and a ticket booth

scenes.text: Imagine a village fair where everything costs one ticket.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A bowl of rice: one ticket. A ride on a camel: one ticket.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Now a rich visitor arrives and hands every family fifty free tickets.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The fair didn't get more rice. It just got more tickets.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So the stall owners raise the price. A bowl of rice now costs two tickets.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Each ticket is worth less, because there are more of them chasing the same stuff.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That's inflation: prices go up because money goes down in value.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Gold works the same way. It's only worth a lot while it's rare.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In Cairo, one gold coin, a mithqal, buys about twenty-five silver coins. Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1324 you set out for Mecca, about four thousand kilometers away.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: camel caravan route across the Sahara desert, 1324: huge sand dunes, a line of tents and camel saddles, a small well, blazing sky

scenes.text: Arab writers later describe thousands of servants dressed in silk.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: camel caravan route across the Sahara desert, 1324: huge sand dunes, a line of tents and camel saddles, a small well, blazing sky

scenes.text: They say about eighty camels carried loads of gold dust.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: camel caravan route across the Sahara desert, 1324: huge sand dunes, a line of tents and camel saddles, a small well, blazing sky

scenes.text: Those numbers are big, round and repeated by people who weren't there.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: camel caravan route across the Sahara desert, 1324: huge sand dunes, a line of tents and camel saddles, a small well, blazing sky

scenes.text: But everybody agrees on one thing: it was a lot of gold.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: camel caravan route across the Sahara desert, 1324: huge sand dunes, a line of tents and camel saddles, a small well, blazing sky

scenes.text: Your wife, Inari Konte, travels with her own court of servants.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: camel caravan route across the Sahara desert, 1324: huge sand dunes, a line of tents and camel saddles, a small well, blazing sky

scenes.text: Crossing the Sahara takes months. Water is worth more than gold out here.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: camel caravan route across the Sahara desert, 1324: huge sand dunes, a line of tents and camel saddles, a small well, blazing sky

scenes.text: The internet says you built a mosque every Friday along the way.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: camel caravan route across the Sahara desert, 1324: huge sand dunes, a line of tents and camel saddles, a small well, blazing sky

scenes.text: That story comes from a chronicle written three centuries later. Nobody can find the mosques.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: camel caravan route across the Sahara desert, 1324: huge sand dunes, a line of tents and camel saddles, a small well, blazing sky

scenes.text: Even for you, that would be a lot of mosques.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: camel caravan route across the Sahara desert, 1324: huge sand dunes, a line of tents and camel saddles, a small well, blazing sky

scenes.text: You camp for three days by the pyramids, outside Cairo.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: camel caravan route across the Sahara desert, 1324: huge sand dunes, a line of tents and camel saddles, a small well, blazing sky

scenes.text: On July 19th, you enter Cairo, one of the biggest cities in the world.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Mamluk sultan's audience hall in the Cairo Citadel, 1324: striped stone arches, marble floor, carved throne platform, brass lamps, silk carpets

scenes.text: The sultan of Egypt, al-Nasir Muhammad, wants to meet you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Mamluk sultan's audience hall in the Cairo Citadel, 1324: striped stone arches, marble floor, carved throne platform, brass lamps, silk carpets

scenes.text: There's a problem. Visitors must kiss the ground in front of the sultan.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Mamluk sultan's audience hall in the Cairo Citadel, 1324: striped stone arches, marble floor, carved throne platform, brass lamps, silk carpets

scenes.text: You're a king too. You don't kiss anybody's floor.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Mamluk sultan's audience hall in the Cairo Citadel, 1324: striped stone arches, marble floor, carved throne platform, brass lamps, silk carpets

scenes.text: For days, you refuse to go. Officials keep politely insisting.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Mamluk sultan's audience hall in the Cairo Citadel, 1324: striped stone arches, marble floor, carved throne platform, brass lamps, silk carpets

scenes.text: Finally you bow, and you tell everyone who you're bowing to.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Mamluk sultan's audience hall in the Cairo Citadel, 1324: striped stone arches, marble floor, carved throne platform, brass lamps, silk carpets

scenes.text: I prostrate myself to God who created me.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Mamluk sultan's audience hall in the Cairo Citadel, 1324: striped stone arches, marble floor, carved throne platform, brass lamps, silk carpets

quote.text: I prostrate myself to God who created me.

scenes.text: A good answer. The sultan seats you beside him, which is a very big deal.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Mamluk sultan's audience hall in the Cairo Citadel, 1324: striped stone arches, marble floor, carved throne platform, brass lamps, silk carpets

scenes.text: He gives you a palace to stay in, and fine horses. Remember the palace.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Mamluk sultan's audience hall in the Cairo Citadel, 1324: striped stone arches, marble floor, carved throne platform, brass lamps, silk carpets

scenes.text: You and your Cairo host become friends. You talk in Arabic, no translator needed.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Mamluk sultan's audience hall in the Cairo Citadel, 1324: striped stone arches, marble floor, carved throne platform, brass lamps, silk carpets

scenes.text: You tell him the story of the king who sailed away, and how you got the throne.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Mamluk sultan's audience hall in the Cairo Citadel, 1324: striped stone arches, marble floor, carved throne platform, brass lamps, silk carpets

scenes.text: The ruler who preceded me did not believe it impossible to reach the ocean's end.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Mamluk sultan's audience hall in the Cairo Citadel, 1324: striped stone arches, marble floor, carved throne platform, brass lamps, silk carpets

quote.text: The ruler who preceded me did not believe it impossible to reach the ocean's end.

scenes.text: Then the gold comes out.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: busy street in medieval Cairo, 1324: sandstone houses with carved wooden balconies, minarets, market awnings, palm trees, bright sun

scenes.text: You give gold to every official at court, to mosques, to the poor.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: busy street in medieval Cairo, 1324: sandstone houses with carved wooden balconies, minarets, market awnings, palm trees, bright sun

scenes.text: Your people buy whatever Cairo sells: silk, slaves, books, horses.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: busy street in medieval Cairo, 1324: sandstone houses with carved wooden balconies, minarets, market awnings, palm trees, bright sun

scenes.text: Shopkeepers figure out fast that you don't ask prices. So prices rise.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gold and money changers' market in medieval Cairo, 1324: small shop counters with balance scales, piles of coins, gold dust in dishes, arched alley

scenes.text: You also tell your new friends that gold grows like a plant in your country.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: busy street in medieval Cairo, 1324: sandstone houses with carved wooden balconies, minarets, market awnings, palm trees, bright sun

scenes.text: It doesn't. But remember those miners? You don't really know how they find it.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: busy street in medieval Cairo, 1324: sandstone houses with carved wooden balconies, minarets, market awnings, palm trees, bright sun

scenes.text: Years later, a scholar named al-Umari comes to Cairo and interviews people who saw you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gold and money changers' market in medieval Cairo, 1324: small shop counters with balance scales, piles of coins, gold dust in dishes, arched alley

scenes.text: This man flooded Cairo with his benefactions.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gold and money changers' market in medieval Cairo, 1324: small shop counters with balance scales, piles of coins, gold dust in dishes, arched alley

quote.text: This man flooded Cairo with his benefactions.

scenes.text: Remember the gold coin worth twenty-five silver coins? In the market, that changes.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gold and money changers' market in medieval Cairo, 1324: small shop counters with balance scales, piles of coins, gold dust in dishes, arched alley

scenes.text: Gold was at a high price in Egypt until they came in that year.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gold and money changers' market in medieval Cairo, 1324: small shop counters with balance scales, piles of coins, gold dust in dishes, arched alley

quote.text: Gold was at a high price in Egypt until they came in that year.

scenes.text: The coin falls below twenty-two silver, and stays down for at least twelve years.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gold and money changers' market in medieval Cairo, 1324: small shop counters with balance scales, piles of coins, gold dust in dishes, arched alley

scenes.text: Like the free tickets at the fair: more gold, same stuff, so each coin buys less.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gold and money changers' market in medieval Cairo, 1324: small shop counters with balance scales, piles of coins, gold dust in dishes, arched alley

scenes.text: The internet says you crashed Egypt's economy for twelve years.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gold and money changers' market in medieval Cairo, 1324: small shop counters with balance scales, piles of coins, gold dust in dishes, arched alley

scenes.text: That's a stretch. A drop of about twelve percent was normal for gold prices back then.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gold and money changers' market in medieval Cairo, 1324: small shop counters with balance scales, piles of coins, gold dust in dishes, arched alley

scenes.text: You moved the gold market in a giant city. You didn't break a country.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gold and money changers' market in medieval Cairo, 1324: small shop counters with balance scales, piles of coins, gold dust in dishes, arched alley

scenes.text: In October, you leave Cairo with the official caravan to Mecca.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: pilgrim camp in the desert hills of Arabia, 1324: rows of white tents, camels resting, rocky hills, evening light, no buildings

scenes.text: You complete the hajj, like millions before and after you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: pilgrim camp in the desert hills of Arabia, 1324: rows of white tents, camels resting, rocky hills, evening light, no buildings

scenes.text: You give generously in the holy cities too.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: pilgrim camp in the desert hills of Arabia, 1324: rows of white tents, camels resting, rocky hills, evening light, no buildings

scenes.text: And you go shopping for something gold can't make: scholars.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: pilgrim camp in the desert hills of Arabia, 1324: rows of white tents, camels resting, rocky hills, evening light, no buildings

scenes.text: You invite learned men to come back with you to Mali.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: pilgrim camp in the desert hills of Arabia, 1324: rows of white tents, camels resting, rocky hills, evening light, no buildings

scenes.text: One of them is a poet from Spain, Abu Ishaq al-Sahili.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: pilgrim camp in the desert hills of Arabia, 1324: rows of white tents, camels resting, rocky hills, evening light, no buildings

scenes.text: He's not an architect. That will matter later, when people tell your story wrong.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: pilgrim camp in the desert hills of Arabia, 1324: rows of white tents, camels resting, rocky hills, evening light, no buildings

scenes.text: On the way home, your caravan gets lost in the desert, and many people die.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: pilgrim camp in the desert hills of Arabia, 1324: rows of white tents, camels resting, rocky hills, evening light, no buildings

scenes.text: When you finally stagger back to Cairo, something is missing. The gold.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You spent it. All of it. The richest king Cairo ever saw is now short of cash.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Cairo merchant's office, 1325: carpets, ledgers on a low desk, money chest, lamp

scenes.text: Your people sell their goods at a loss, just to eat.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So you do what kings do. You borrow.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A merchant family, led by Siraj al-Din, lends you fifty thousand gold dinars.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That's more than two hundred kilos of gold, well over ten million dollars today.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: At high interest, of course. Lenders can see when a king is desperate.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember the palace the sultan gave you? You sell it to the lenders.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The man who handed out gold in July is pawning his house by spring.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The gold you spent in Cairo made gold cheap. Now you're buying it back.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You make it home in 1325, with no gold, many debts, and a city of scholars.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Timbuktu, 1330: earthen mud-brick mosque under construction with wooden beams sticking out of the walls, sandy square, palm-wood ladders

scenes.text: Your empire now includes Timbuktu, a trading town on the edge of the Sahara.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Timbuktu, 1330: earthen mud-brick mosque under construction with wooden beams sticking out of the walls, sandy square, palm-wood ladders

scenes.text: You order a great mosque built there, the Djinguereber Mosque.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Timbuktu, 1330: earthen mud-brick mosque under construction with wooden beams sticking out of the walls, sandy square, palm-wood ladders

scenes.text: Its walls are mud brick, with wooden beams sticking out to hold the scaffolding.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Timbuktu, 1330: earthen mud-brick mosque under construction with wooden beams sticking out of the walls, sandy square, palm-wood ladders

scenes.text: You also pay your poet friend twelve thousand gold coins for a royal audience hall.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Timbuktu, 1330: earthen mud-brick mosque under construction with wooden beams sticking out of the walls, sandy square, palm-wood ladders

scenes.text: That's about fifty kilos of gold, for a poet who isn't an architect.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Timbuktu, 1330: earthen mud-brick mosque under construction with wooden beams sticking out of the walls, sandy square, palm-wood ladders

scenes.text: Later writers will say he designed all of Mali's famous mosques. He didn't.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Timbuktu, 1330: earthen mud-brick mosque under construction with wooden beams sticking out of the walls, sandy square, palm-wood ladders

scenes.text: Mud-brick building in West Africa is older than him, and older than you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Timbuktu, 1330: earthen mud-brick mosque under construction with wooden beams sticking out of the walls, sandy square, palm-wood ladders

scenes.text: Timbuktu fills with teachers, judges and astronomers, and with their books.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Timbuktu, 1330: earthen mud-brick mosque under construction with wooden beams sticking out of the walls, sandy square, palm-wood ladders

scenes.text: In 1330, a neighboring kingdom raids Timbuktu. You take it back and build a fort.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Timbuktu, 1330: earthen mud-brick mosque under construction with wooden beams sticking out of the walls, sandy square, palm-wood ladders

scenes.text: Back in Cairo, Siraj al-Din is still waiting for his fifty thousand dinars.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gold and money changers' market in medieval Cairo, 1324: small shop counters with balance scales, piles of coins, gold dust in dishes, arched alley

scenes.text: So he sends a man across the desert to Mali to collect.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gold and money changers' market in medieval Cairo, 1324: small shop counters with balance scales, piles of coins, gold dust in dishes, arched alley

scenes.text: The man dies in Timbuktu before he collects anything.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Timbuktu, 1330: earthen mud-brick mosque under construction with wooden beams sticking out of the walls, sandy square, palm-wood ladders

scenes.text: Later, Siraj al-Din's son makes the trip and gets some of the money back.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Arab historians disagree on how much was ever repaid. Some say most of it never was.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Lending to a king two months away by camel is a special kind of risk.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Sometime around 1337, after about twenty-five years as mansa, you die.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: royal court of the Mali Empire, about 1300: large round mud-brick audience hall with a thatched roof, carved wooden stools, drums, silk canopy, courtyard

scenes.text: Nobody even agrees on the year. It might be 1332.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: royal court of the Mali Empire, about 1300: large round mud-brick audience hall with a thatched roof, carved wooden stools, drums, silk canopy, courtyard

scenes.text: Your son Maghan becomes mansa. Within a few generations, Mali's empire shrinks.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: royal court of the Mali Empire, about 1300: large round mud-brick audience hall with a thatched roof, carved wooden stools, drums, silk canopy, courtyard

scenes.text: Ibn Battuta visits Mali in 1352 and finds your brother on the throne.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: royal court of the Mali Empire, about 1300: large round mud-brick audience hall with a thatched roof, carved wooden stools, drums, silk canopy, courtyard

scenes.text: The famous traveler complains he's stingy. So much for the family reputation.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: royal court of the Mali Empire, about 1300: large round mud-brick audience hall with a thatched roof, carved wooden stools, drums, silk canopy, courtyard

scenes.text: But Europe doesn't forget you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: mapmaker's workshop in Majorca, 1375: big hand-painted world map spread on a wooden table, ink pots, quills, compasses, arched window over the sea

scenes.text: In 1375, a mapmaker in Majorca paints a huge map of the known world.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: mapmaker's workshop in Majorca, 1375: big hand-painted world map spread on a wooden table, ink pots, quills, compasses, arched window over the sea

scenes.text: In the middle of Africa, he paints you: on a throne, holding a big gold nugget.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: mapmaker's workshop in Majorca, 1375: big hand-painted world map spread on a wooden table, ink pots, quills, compasses, arched window over the sea

scenes.text: Next to you, he writes a note.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: mapmaker's workshop in Majorca, 1375: big hand-painted world map spread on a wooden table, ink pots, quills, compasses, arched window over the sea

scenes.text: So abundant is the gold, he writes, you're the richest and most noble king in the land.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: mapmaker's workshop in Majorca, 1375: big hand-painted world map spread on a wooden table, ink pots, quills, compasses, arched window over the sea

paper.text: THE RICHEST AND MOST NOBLE KING

scenes.text: Your Cairo spending spree became your advertisement.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: mapmaker's workshop in Majorca, 1375: big hand-painted world map spread on a wooden table, ink pots, quills, compasses, arched window over the sea

scenes.text: For two hundred years, Europeans dream about the gold of Mali.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: mapmaker's workshop in Majorca, 1375: big hand-painted world map spread on a wooden table, ink pots, quills, compasses, arched window over the sea

scenes.text: Now, the internet's favorite fact: you were the richest person in history.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Some websites say four hundred billion dollars. Some say your wealth is impossible to count.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The honest answer is the second one. Nobody wrote down your treasury.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You didn't own the mines. You taxed them. Remember?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And you couldn't even pay your own bills in Cairo.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Rich? Spectacularly. Richest ever? Nobody can know.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So how does the richest-looking man in Cairo end up borrowing from its merchants?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He spent faster than he could earn, in a city where his gold was losing value.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Every coin he gave away made the next coin worth a little less.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And he was buying with that cheaper gold.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That brings us to today's money rule.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: MONEY RULE: PRICES FOLLOW THE MONEY

scenes.bgIdea: modern bank branch, 2020s

scenes.text: When money grows faster than the things it buys, each unit buys less.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Here's a recent example. Between 2020 and 2022, the US money supply grew about forty percent.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In June 2022, prices were up nine percent in a single year.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Say your boss gave you a three percent raise that year.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your paycheck grew three percent. Your rent and groceries grew about eight.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You got a raise and still got poorer.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So when you ask for a raise, compare it to prices, not to last year's paycheck.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And the rule isn't perfect. Cairo's gold barely dropped twelve percent.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: When more things are made too, more money doesn't have to mean higher prices.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Even Mansa Musa's gold couldn't buy what Cairo didn't have.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Spend like a king, and the price of everything learns your name.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.title: YOUR LIFE AS MANSA MUSA

meta.thumbnail: A Cairo street in 1324 with a camel caravan and gold dust in the air; text: 'TOO MUCH GOLD'
meta.description:
It's 1324. You ride into Cairo with so much gold that it changes what gold is worth in Egypt.
A few months later, you're borrowing money there. This is the life of Mansa Musa.

A comedic dramatization of documented history.
General education only, not financial advice.

Sources:
- Mansa Musa, Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansa_Musa
- Al-Umari, Masalik al-Absar, in N. Levtzion and J. F. P. Hopkins (eds.), Corpus of Early Arabic Sources for West African History (1981)
- Ibn Khaldun, Kitab al-Ibar, in Levtzion and Hopkins (1981)
- Catalan Atlas (1375), Bibliotheque nationale de France, Espagnol 30
- US Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI-U (June 2022); Federal Reserve, M2 money stock
factCheck: Born about 1280 (exact date unknown); reigned c. 1312 to c. 1337, about 25 years per Ibn Khaldun; death year disputed (1332 or 1337) (Wikipedia).
Descendant of Sunjata's family; Ibn Khaldun calls him Musa ibn Abu Bakr; exact lineage DISPUTED (Wikipedia). 'Great-uncle's family' is a simplification.
Mansa means ruler/king in Mandinka (Wikipedia).

Gold fields of Bambuk and Bure; Mali kings taxed gold and reserved nuggets for themselves, merchants traded dust (al-Umari via Levtzion & Hopkins; widely cited). Claim that gold production stopped when rulers tried to convert or control miners comes from al-Umari: DISPUTED.
Salt traded 'weight for weight' with gold: popular exaggeration, flagged as such in the script.

Predecessor's Atlantic voyages: 200 ships then 2,000, Musa left as deputy; told by Musa in Cairo to Ibn Amir Hajib, recorded by al-Umari; predecessor presumably Muhammad ibn Qu; the name Abubakari II and the America claim are modern: DISPUTED (Wikipedia).
Gao taken by general Saghmanja (Ibn Khaldun); Musa claimed 24 cities in Cairo (Wikipedia).

Hajj 1324-1325; camped three days near Giza, entered Cairo 19 July 1324, left 18 October with the official caravan (Wikipedia). Distance Niani-Mecca roughly 4,000 km (journey given as about 2,700 miles).
Caravan: thousands of servants in silk, about 80 camels with gold dust: figures from later Arabic accounts, rhetorical, DISPUTED (Wikipedia). Wife Inari Konte (Wikipedia).
'Mosque every Friday' from the Tarikh al-Sudan (17th century): DISPUTED (Wikipedia).
Refused to prostrate before Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad, then said he prostrated to God; seated beside the sultan; given a palace (al-Umari via Wikipedia).
Told people in Cairo gold grew like a plant in his country (Wikipedia).
Gold mithqal fell from 25 dirhams to under 22 and did not recover for at least 12 years (al-Umari); Warren Schultz argues the fall was within normal Mamluk fluctuation; ~12% = 3/25 (Wikipedia).
Caravan lost in the desert on return with many deaths (al-Umari, widely cited): DISPUTED in detail.

Ran short of money, sold goods at a loss, borrowed at high interest; Siraj al-Din ibn al-Kuwayk lent 50,000 dinars; Musa sold him the palace; Siraj's agent died trying to collect; son Fakhr al-Din recovered some; repayment DISPUTED (Wikipedia). 50,000 dinars x ~4.25 g = ~212 kg of gold; at over $60 per gram that is over $10 million today.
Djinguereber Mosque commissioned 1327; al-Sahili paid 12,000 mithqals (about 51 kg) for a royal audience chamber; idea that al-Sahili designed Mali's mosques is a historiographical myth (Wikipedia).
Mossi took Timbuktu in 1330; Musa retook it and built a fort (Wikipedia).
Successor Maghan; Ibn Battuta visited Mali 1352 under Mansa Sulayman, Musa's brother, and found him stingy (Ibn Battuta, Rihla).
Catalan Atlas 1375 by Abraham Cresques in Majorca shows Musa holding a gold nugget; inscription calls him the richest and most noble king in all the land because of the abundance of gold (BnF).
$400 billion figure comes from modern websites; historians say his wealth cannot be calculated (Time, quoting Richard Smith).

US M2 rose from about $15.4 trillion (Feb 2020) to about $21.7 trillion (early 2022), about +40% (Federal Reserve). CPI-U +9.1% year over year in June 2022 and about 8% for 2022 (BLS). Raise example is illustrative.
sources: 'I prostrate myself to God who created me.': Mansa Musa as reported by al-Umari, Masalik al-Absar, in Levtzion & Hopkins, Corpus of Early Arabic Sources for West African History (1981)
'The ruler who preceded me did not believe it impossible to reach the ocean's end.': shortened from Mansa Musa's account in al-Umari, Masalik al-Absar (Levtzion & Hopkins 1981)
'This man flooded Cairo with his benefactions.': al-Umari, Masalik al-Absar (Levtzion & Hopkins 1981)
'Gold was at a high price in Egypt until they came in that year.': al-Umari, Masalik al-Absar (Levtzion & Hopkins 1981)
Catalan Atlas (1375), BnF Espagnol 30: inscription on Musse Melly, 'the richest and most noble king in all the land'
Ibn Battuta, Rihla (1355), visit to Mali 1352-1353
Time, 'Meet Mansa Musa I of Mali', 2015 (Richard Smith quote)
